ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows a single-phase uncontrolled diode bridge rectifier. The AC source is labeled 220 V, 50 Hz and is connected through a source inductance labeled Ls = 10 mH to the bridge AC terminals. The DC side has a constant-current load labeled Io = 14 A. The bridge diodes are labeled D1 and D3 at the upper positions, and D4 and D2 at the lower positions; D1 is one of the bridge diodes. Reasoning: Take the supply voltage as vs = Vm sinθ, where Vm = sqrt(2) × 220 = 311.13 V and ω = 2π × 50 = 314.16 rad/s. Because of the source inductance, current transfer during commutation is not instantaneous. At the natural commutation instant for D1, the source current must change by 2Io = 28 A during the overlap interval μ. Using the assigned overlap relation, ∫0^μ Vm sinθ dθ = 2ωLsIo. Thus Vm(1 − cos μ) = 2ωLsIo. Substituting Ls = 0.01 H and Io = 14 A gives 311.13(1 − cos μ) = 2 × 314.16 × 0.01 × 14 = 87.96. Hence 1 − cos μ = 0.2827, so cos μ = 0.7173 and μ = 44.17°. The conduction angle of D1 is 180° + μ = 180° + 44.17° = 224.17°.
